ModMetadata.Name: IZCode
ModMetadata.Author: julianobd
ModMetadata.Description:
[h1]IZCode - Structured Programming for Stationeers[/h1]
IZCode replaces IC10 with IZ: a structured programming language with types, real functions and recursion, running on its own virtual machine inside the Programmable Chip.
Write [b]#iz[/b] on the first line of a chip and IZCode takes over. Chips without the marker continue working as normal IC10, so existing builds are unaffected.
[h2]WHY IT EXISTS[/h2]
[table] [tr][th]IC10[/th][th]IZ[/th][/tr] [tr][td]128 lines, 4096 bytes[/td][td]2000 lines, 16000 bytes[/td][/tr] [tr][td]16 registers[/td][td]Named variables managed by the compiler[/td][/tr] [tr][td]jal/ra, limited calls[/td][td]Functions, parameters, returns and recursion[/td][/tr] [tr][td]Restarts every tick[/td][td]Freezes and resumes execution[/td][/tr] [tr][td]Infinite loop hangs the chip[/td][td]VM preempts execution automatically[/td][/tr] [tr][td]Typos found at runtime[/td][td]Compile errors with suggestions[/td][/tr] [tr][td]Everything is a double[/td][td]num, bool, str and dev are type-checked[/td][/tr] [tr][td]HASH("text")[/td][td]Real strings with concatenation and comparison[/td][/tr] [tr][td]Loose registers[/td][td]Arrays, structs and lists[/td][/tr] [/table]
[h2]A COMPLETE PROGRAM[/h2]
[code] #iz device sensor = d0; device inlet = d1;
const TARGET = 101.325;
fn main() { loop { var p = sensor.Pressure; inlet.On = p < TARGET - 5.0; yield; } } [/code]
Execution starts at [b]fn main()[/b]. When it returns, the chip stops until restarted.
[h2]THE LANGUAGE[/h2]
[h3]Types[/h3]
[list] [*][b]num[/b] — 64-bit floating-point number [*][b]bool[/b] — Boolean value [*][b]str[/b] — Immutable ASCII string [*][b]dev[/b] — Device pin d0-d5, or db [*][b]T[N][/b] — Fixed-size arrays [*][b]list[/b] — Typed collections [*][b]struct[/b] — User-defined structures [/list]
num and bool are not interchangeable. [code]if x[/code] requires a bool; write [code]if x != 0[/code] for numeric conditions.
[code] var counter = 0; var active: bool = false; const MAX = 101.325; [/code]
Globals keep their values across ticks.
[h3]Arrays and Structs[/h3]
Arrays and structs live in the VM heap and are laid out at compile time. There is no runtime allocator or garbage collector.
[code] var samples: num[8];
struct Gauge { total: num; cursor: num; samples: num[8]; } [/code]
Array length is part of the type, and [code]len(a)[/code] is resolved at compile time. Aggregates are passed by reference. Recursive calls get their own local storage.
[h3]Lists and Queries[/h3]
Lists are fixed-size arrays with a count, providing LINQ-style queries:
[code] var rooms: list Room[8];
var r: Room; r.temp = 40; rooms.add(r);
var mean = rooms.avg(x => x.temp); var hot = rooms.where(x => x.temp > 30); var worst = rooms.orderByDesc(x => x.temp).first(); [/code]
[b]Queries:[/b]
[list] [*]where, select, take, skip [*]takeWhile, skipWhile [*]orderBy, orderByDesc, reverse [*]distinct, sum, avg, min, max [*]count, any, all [*]first, last, firstOr, lastOr [*]contains, indexOf, into [/list]
Query chains become a single loop. Lambdas are inlined, avoiding intermediate lists and per-element calls.
[h3]Devices[/h3]
Device properties are checked against the game's LogicType table:
[code] var p = sensor.Pressure; pump.On = true; [/code]
Invalid properties produce compile-time errors with suggestions:
[code] Presure [/code]
[b]Error:[/b] Unknown device property. Did you mean [b]Pressure?[/b]
[b]db[/b] is the device the chip is installed in, and the only way to reach it: nothing can be wired to it. In a circuit housing it is the housing; in a hardsuit, which holds a chip in its own slot, it is the suit, so a program can read its own PressureExternal and drive its AC. On a suit the six pins are the wearer's slots: d0 helmet, d1 backpack, d2 toolbelt, d3 glasses, d4 and d5 hands.
[code] device self = db; self.Setting = 1; [/code]
[h3]Batch Operations[/h3]
Operate on every matching device on the data network:
[code] all(StructureWallLight).On = true; named("Corridor Light").On = false; named(StructureVolumePump, "north").On = true;
var avg = all(StructureGasSensor).Pressure; [/code]
A selector can also be given a name, and is then used like a device on a pin:
[code] device led = named(StructureDiode, #"led-dev"); led.On = true; [/code]
Prefab names, [code]#"hash"[/code] literals and constants are compile-time values with zero runtime cost.
[h3]Text[/h3]
Strings are real runtime values and can be stored in variables, parameters, returns, arrays and structs.
[code] var label = "vent-" + side; all("Structure" + kind).On = true; [/code]
[b]Functions:[/b] [b]len[/b], [b]hash[/b], [b]char[/b], [b]chr[/b], [b]sub[/b], [b]find[/b], [b]text[/b], [b]fixed[/b], [b]parse[/b].
Numbers become text only through [code]text(x)[/code].
[h3]Control Flow[/h3]
[list] [*]if / else if / else [*]while / loop [*]for [*]break / continue [/list]
Ranges support [code]0..10[/code] and [code]0..=10[/code]. There is no goto or labels. Braces are mandatory.
[h3]Functions and Recursion[/h3]
Functions have typed parameters, return values and recursion.
[code] fn gcd(a: num, b: num) -> num { if b == 0 { return a; } return gcd(b, a % b); } [/code]
Recursion is protected by a call-depth limit with a clean runtime error.
[h3]Operators and Math[/h3]
Operators follow C precedence. Prefix operators include [b]-x[/b], [b]!x[/b] and [b]~x[/b].
Division by zero follows IEEE-754. Assignment is a statement, so [code]if (a = b)[/code] does not compile.
Math and trigonometry functions are available, along with [b]len[/b], [b]hash[/b], [b]rand[/b], [b]nan[/b] and [b]inf[/b].
[h3]Tick Control[/h3]
[code]yield[/code] gives the tick back and resumes at the next instruction.
[code]sleep(2)[/code] suspends execution.
Without either, the VM automatically preempts execution when the budget is reached.
[h2]THE EDITOR, UPGRADED[/h2]
[h3]Real Code Area[/h3]
The standard Stationeers editor uses 128 independent text fields. IZ mode turns it into one proper editor with a gutter and current-line highlight.
[list] [*]Drag selection [*]Shift + Arrow [*]Ctrl + A / C / X / V [*]Mouse wheel [*]VS Code-style indentation [/list]
[h3]Wiring-Aware Completion[/h3]
The editor knows which device is connected to each pin. Typing [code]pump.[/code] suggests the properties of that specific device, including live values.
It also completes pins, prefab names, slot properties, list queries and your own declarations.
[h3]Live Errors[/h3]
The same compiler used by the chip analyzes the editor shortly after you stop typing.
[list] [*]Red underline — errors [*]Amber underline — warnings [*]Diagnostic panel with details [/list]
Runtime errors light the housing's error LED, like an IC10 exception.
[h3]Hover Information[/h3]
Hover over a device variable to see its equipment, label, hash and readable properties.
[h2]REQUIREMENTS[/h2]
IZCode is a C# plugin. Stationeers requires a mod loader to run it.
[list] [*]BepInEx [*]StationeersLaunchPad [*]IZCode [/list]
Enable IZCode in the mods menu. [code][IZCode][/code] in [code]Player.log[/code] confirms that it loaded.
[h2]SAFE TO TRY[/h2]
Because [code]#iz[/code] is a valid comment to the IC10 parser, a chip containing IZ code does not break for players who do not have IZCode installed.
Example programs are included in [code]samples/[/code], covering pressure control, solar tracking, list queries and a full hardsuit controller.
[h2]MULTIPLAYER[/h2]
[b]Multiplayer has NOT been tested.[/b]
Every client and the server need the mod installed, and VM behavior in multiplayer is currently unknown. Use it at your own risk and report your findings on the issue tracker.
[h2]LINKS[/h2]
[b]Source code:[/b] [url=https://github.com/julianobd/IZCode]GitHub Repository[/url]
[b]Bug reports:[/b] [url=https://github.com/julianobd/IZCode/issues]Issue Tracker[/url]

ModMetadata.ChangeLog:
===== 0.1.4 =========================================================
BIGGER PROGRAMS. The editor's 128 lines of 90 characters, 4096 bytes in all, are the size of the game's own input fields. In IZ mode the code area is what holds the program and what gets saved comes from there, so the ceiling is now 2000 lines of 200 characters, 16000 bytes - as much as TextMeshPro can draw. Deleting the '#iz' marker no longer costs what is past the 128th line: type it again and the program comes back whole.
COPY, PASTE AND CLEAR. The three buttons wrote straight into the 128 lines, and the code area put its own text back over them on the next frame, so they looked inert. They work now, and carry the whole program: pasting a 400 line script keeps its 400 lines.
